reasons: The file says tests check that every key exists in every language, but those tests are not visible in the packet.
A missing placeholder value is not reported as an error.

terms.meaning: Preparing the app so its text can be shown in several languages.
A language and region setting, such as English or Hindi.
The fixed name of one message, used to look up its text in each language.
A marked spot in a message, such as a name in braces, that is filled in when the message is shown.
A small saved value that the browser sends back to the site on each visit.

sections.name: LANGS, Lang
sections.title: Supported languages
sections.what: Lists the two supported languages, English and Hindi, and defines the type that stands for a language code.
sections.why: The header says English is the source and Hindi covers the Desk and navigation.
sections.watch_out: Adding a language here without messages for every key will break the page.

sections.name: isLang
sections.title: Language check and cookie name
sections.what: Checks whether a value is a supported language and names the cookie that stores the visitor's choice.
sections.why: Stops a bad or changed cookie from loading a language the app does not have.
sections.watch_out: Renaming the cookie resets every visitor's language, and the proxy file reads the same name.

sections.name: en, MessageKey
sections.title: English messages
sections.what: The master list of every message key with its English text, covering navigation, the Desk, receipts, sport names and pending notes.
sections.why: English is the source, so every other language is checked against this list.
sections.watch_out: A new message key must be added here first, because the key type is taken from this list.

sections.name: hi, MESSAGES
sections.title: Hindi messages
sections.what: Hindi text for each English key, with placeholders kept in braces.
sections.why: Hindi covers the Desk and navigation, as the header notes.
sections.watch_out: Placeholders must match the English text exactly, or the filled message will be wrong.

sections.name: t, messageKeys
sections.title: Looking up a message
sections.what: Returns the message for a language and fills in its placeholders. Also lists every key for a language.
sections.why: One function means every page formats text the same way.
sections.watch_out: A placeholder with no value is left in braces on screen, so every caller must pass all its values.

summary: The language setup: supported languages, the cookie that remembers a visitor's choice, and the English and Hindi wording for the app's messages.
purpose: It lets the app show its text in English or Hindi, starting with the Desk and navigation.
why: English is the source text and Hindi is translated from it, so every key must exist in both.
how: It lists the two languages and checks a value against that list. It stores the English messages as the master list, then the Hindi messages typed to match every key. A lookup function fills in placeholders such as team names, and another function lists the keys for a language.
inputs: A language code, a message key, and optional values to fill into placeholders.
outputs: The message text in the chosen language, or the list of message keys.
risks: A message key missing from Hindi is caught by the type checker, but a missing placeholder value leaves braces showing on screen.
debug: If text shows braces such as a name in curly brackets, check the caller passes every value. If a language is not recognised, check the cookie name and the value stored in it.
